fact: Labradors come from Newfoundland, not Labrador, where their ancestors helped fishermen haul in nets.
A Lab's thick otter tail works like a rudder when it swims.
French Bulldogs began with lace makers in Nottingham, England, who took their little bulldogs with them to France.
American breeders in the 1890s insisted on the bat ears, and the bat ears won.
Golden Retrievers were developed in the Scottish Highlands in the 1800s by Lord Tweedmouth.
Goldens were bred with a soft mouth, so they could carry a bird back without a mark on it.
The German Shepherd was developed in 1899 by Max von Stephanitz, a cavalry officer.
Rin Tin Tin, a German Shepherd rescued from a World War I battlefield, became a Hollywood star.
Poodles were water retrievers first. The name comes from the German word for splashing in water.
The famous poodle clip started as a practical one: it kept the joints and chest warm in cold water.
Bulldogs are named for bull baiting, a sport England banned in 1835.
Yale's bulldog, Handsome Dan, is often called the first live mascot of an American university.
Snoopy is a Beagle.
The Beagle Brigade sniffs luggage at US airports for the Department of Agriculture.
Rottweilers are named for the German town of Rottweil, where they drove cattle to market.
Butchers in Rottweil are said to have tied their money pouches to their dogs' collars for safekeeping.
Dachshund means badger dog in German.
A Dachshund named Waldi was the first official Olympic mascot, at the Munich games in 1972.
The German Shorthaired Pointer was bred to point, retrieve and track, all in one dog.
Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 Pembroke Welsh Corgis.
Corgis herded cattle by nipping at their heels, staying low enough to duck the kicks.
The Cardigan is the Corgi with the long tail.
Despite the name, the Australian Shepherd was developed in the American West.
Aussies became famous as rodeo dogs in the 1950s and 1960s.
Yorkies were bred in northern England to catch rats in the textile mills.
A Yorkie named Smoky served with US troops in World War II and is often called the first therapy dog.
The breed is named for King Charles II, who was rarely seen without his spaniels.
Louis Dobermann, a German tax collector, developed the breed in the 1890s to keep him safe on his rounds.
Cane Corsos nearly disappeared in the 20th century and were brought back by Italian enthusiasts in the 1970s.
Schnauzer comes from the German word for snout, a nod to that famous beard.
Miniature Schnauzers were bred as ratters on German farms.
Boxers are said to be named for the way they stand up and bat with their front paws.
Despite the name, the Great Dane is German, not Danish.
Scooby-Doo is a Great Dane.
A Great Dane named Zeus is the tallest dog on record, at 44 inches at the shoulder.
Shih Tzu means little lion in Chinese.
Shih Tzus were palace dogs of Chinese royalty for centuries.
In 1925, sled dogs, Huskies among them, carried diphtheria medicine 674 miles to Nome, Alaska.
Bernese Mountain Dogs pulled carts of milk and cheese for Swiss farmers.
Two of the three dogs that survived the Titanic were Pomeranians.
The Boston Terrier was one of the first breeds developed in the United States.
The Boston Terrier is the official state dog of Massachusetts.
The Havanese is the national dog of Cuba.
Shelties come from the Shetland Islands, where the ponies and the sheep run small too.
Springers are named for the way they spring birds into the air for hunters.
A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 toys.
Border Collies herd with an intense stare that breeders call the eye.
The Chihuahua is named for the Mexican state of Chihuahua.
Vizslas are nicknamed Velcro dogs because they stick so close to their people.
Basset comes from the French word bas, meaning low.
Only the Bloodhound is usually ranked above the Basset Hound for scenting ability.
A Belgian Malinois named Cairo was part of the Navy SEAL team on the 2011 Abbottabad raid.
Maltese have been lap dogs for more than 2,000 years, praised by ancient Greek and Roman writers.
Weimaraners are called the Gray Ghost for their silver coat and quiet way of hunting.
Lassie was played by a line of male Rough Collies, starting with a dog named Pal.
Newfoundlands have webbed feet and a water resistant coat, and they're famous for water rescue.
Ridgebacks were bred in southern Africa and were once known as African Lion Hounds.
The dog in the Doge meme was a Shiba Inu named Kabosu.
The Shiba is the smallest of Japan's six native breeds.
A pug named Pompey is said to have saved William of Orange by barking at assassins in 1572.
Pugs come from China, where they were companions to emperors.
The first Labradoodle was bred in Australia in 1989, to be a guide dog for a woman whose husband had allergies.
Goldendoodles took off in the 1990s, following the Labradoodle's lead.
